title: Who are you?
briefing: You have been given access to a Linux machine.
tips: This is a terminal: type a command, press Enter, the machine answers.
Linux commands are short words. Some of them are literally questions.
objective: Find out which user you are logged in as.
expert_objective: Identify the account this shell runs as.
hints: You want to ask the machine a question about yourself. Commands are often English words squashed together.
Ask it literally: who... am... i? All one word, lowercase.

reactions.say: Typos happen to everyone. When a command doesn't exist, the shell tries to guess what you meant — read its suggestion.

explanation: `whoami` prints the account you are using: player. Your prompt says it too — player@workstation:~$ means WHO you are, on WHICH machine, and WHERE. Every file and every process belongs to a user, and every permission check asks one question: who is this? You are not root. Remember that.
